players.product: PCIe Gen6 fabric switches (Scorpio), retimers (Aries), AECs (Torus), CXL memory controllers (Leo) for AI racks

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 RESULTS (call): CEO Jitendra Mohan reported Q4 revenue of $270.6 million, up 17% from the prior quarter and up 92% versus Q4 of last year, and full-year 2025 revenue of $852.5 million, up 115%, with growth 'broad-based, across our signal conditioning, smart cable module, and switch fabric product portfolios' and several new design wins across multiple customers. CFO Mike Tate: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin 75.7%, down 70 basis points on a higher mix of hardware sales; non-GAAP operating margin 40.2%; non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.58; Q4 operating cash flow $95.3 million and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $1.19 billion. Q4 non-GAAP opex rose to $96 million as R&D expanded, including the XScale acquisition that closed during the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $270.6 million (up 17% QoQ, up 92% YoY); FY2025 $852.5 million (up 115%); non-GAAP GM 75.7%; op margin 40.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 GUIDANCE AND AN OPEX STEP-UP: Q1 revenue guided to $286 million to $297 million, up roughly 6% to 10% from Q4. Drivers named by CFO Mike Tate: Aries growth across a variety of AI platforms in both scale-up and scale-out; Taurus growth from higher volumes of 400 gig designs for AI scale-up connectivity; Scorpio growth primarily from continued P Series deployment for scale-out plus initial volumes of Scorpio X Series for scale-up switching. Non-GAAP gross margin approximately 74% on a higher mix of hardware-based solutions; non-GAAP opex approximately $112 million to $118 million, non-GAAP EPS approximately $0.53 to $0.54. Management said customers are presenting 'significant revenue opportunities' and the TAM is 'much bigger than we originally expected' when measured 'twelve, eighteen months ago', so opex rises: a full quarter of the XScale acquisition plus an acqui-hire closed this quarter to scale a new Israel advanced design center (ASIC engineering focused on AI fabrics, custom AI fabric and AI inference technology). Tate put time from start to revenue at 'eighteen, twenty-four months on the earlier side'. Leadership: Mike Tate moves to a full-time strategic adviser role and Desmond Lynch joins as CFO effective March 2.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 guide $286 million to $297 million (up roughly 6% to 10%); GM approximately 74%; opex $112 million to $118 million; EPS $0.53 to $0.54

quarterly_data.signal: SCORPIO STATUS AT THE START OF 2026: Scorpio P Series (scale-out PCIe 6 switching) beat its 10% bogey and crossed above 15% of 2025 revenue, and management called it 'the only PCIe six fabric shipping in volume in the market' ('we are probably still the only one that's in high volume production with our Gen six switches'). Scorpio P design wins now include two NEW hyperscalers - confirmed as US when asked - going into production toward the end of 2026 on platforms that are 'both merchant GPU-based as well as custom accelerators', expected to add meaningful revenue in 2027; asked whether they can match the lead hyperscaler, Mohan said 'There is a potential for that.' Scorpio X Series (scale-up) shipped preproduction quantities in Q4, starts initial volumes in 1H 2026 with 'a much more material ramp in the back half of the year' at the lead customer; Astera is engaged with 10 plus customers on Scorpio X, expects some to qualify toward the end of 2026 and volume ramps in 2027. Together P and X put Scorpio on a trajectory to become the biggest product line, timing not fixed.
quarterly_data.figure: Scorpio P crossed above 15% of 2025 revenue (10% bogey); 10 plus Scorpio X customers; new-customer X volume ramps set for 2027

quarterly_data.signal: SIGNAL CONDITIONING - PCIe 6 AND 400G-TO-800G TRANSITIONS: the Aries retimer portfolio (printed 'Ares' in the transcript) grew nearly 70% year over year in 2025, driven by custom AI accelerator deployments at large hyperscalers; Aries Gen 6 is 'the industry's only PCIe six DSP retimer solution shipping to customers in high volume today', and in Q4 Astera began shipping PCIe Gen 6 smart cable modules for scale-up topologies in high volume - cabled PCIe 'does give us an uplift in the ASP'. Management expects more customers to launch PCIe 6 accelerators and systems through 2026 and into 2027. Taurus was the strongest family in 2025, revenue up more than four times year over year on 400 gig designs; Astera sells the modules inside AEC cable assemblies through cable partners, so it comes in as volume builds, and it named the transition to 800 gig switching platforms as the next catalyst - 800 gig qualification is under way with 'multiple customers that are using AEC for 800 gigs'. Current development stretches to 'PCIe Gen seven, UV link 200 gig, and 1.6 Ethernet applications' (as printed).
quarterly_data.figure: Aries nearly 70% year over year in 2025; Taurus revenue more than four times year over year; 400 gig to 800 gig next

quarterly_data.signal: TAM RESET: Mohan estimated Astera's served addressable market will expand by more than 10 times over the next five years to reach $25 billion, spanning existing and announced copper-based families (Aries and Taurus signal conditioning, Scorpio fabric switches, CXL memory controllers (printed 'USCXL') and the new custom scale-up solution). President/COO Sanjay Gajendra sized the merchant scale-up switching market at roughly $20 billion annually by 2030, with the PCIe, UALink and platform-specific roadmap positioning Astera to service 'at least half of this market' near to medium term; optical scale-up connectivity 'could more than double the merchant scale-up switching opportunity'. Backdrop cited by management: Google and AWS alone guiding nearly $400 billion in total 2026 capex.
quarterly_data.figure: SAM more than 10 times over the next five years to reach $25 billion; merchant scale-up switching roughly $20 billion annually by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: OPTICAL ROADMAP TIMING: Astera is working with key customers to define and build silicon-photonics optical connectivity engines for scale-up; Mohan said 'the optical for scale-up, the timing should be somewhere in 2028', and that 'the initial deployment for optical technology CPO might happen with scale-out, and that might precede the deployment of scale-up'. Expected path: pluggable optics, then near-package optics (printed 'a new package optics'), then co-packaged optics - 'we expect to see the first deployments of co-package optics for scale-up sometime in the 2028 time frame' - while 'most of our customers will continue to stay with copper for as long as they can' and 'copper and optical will continue to coexist for a long period of time'. The optical scale-up opportunity is 'Probably larger than the signal conditioning opportunity that we have'. The high-density connectors from the XScale acquisition 'are seeing strong interest and are being qualified for scale-up applications'.
quarterly_data.figure: optical scale-up somewhere in 2028; first co-packaged optics for scale-up in the 2028 time frame

quarterly_data.signal: NVLINK FUSION CUSTOM CONNECTIVITY: in Q4 Astera added custom connectivity solutions whose initial prospects 'will help to enable NVIDIA's NVLink fusion scale-up architecture for hybrid racks', with more hyperscalers in view; Mohan said both Amazon and NVIDIA have chosen Astera as a partner. The part translates the XPU's native protocol into NVLink and attaches one-to-one per XPU, so versus a shared native UALink switch the attach rate is higher and the ASP lower - 'the opportunity is roughly the same for both' - and it 'opens up a completely new set of opportunities for us to play in the NVLink ecosystem', additive to the rest of the plan (commercial terms withheld under NDAs). Content per accelerator keeps rising: 'every generation of XPU, our content has grown up so far'.

BLACKWELL-TO-RUBIN CONTENT DEPENDS ON CUSTOM DEPLOYMENTS: asked how Astera content changes from Blackwell to Vera Rubin, Mohan said the opportunity 'arises when our customers do custom deployments of the Grace Blackwell or in the future, Vera Rubin reference design. We have very minimal opportunity with the reference design itself.' The initial ramps came from customized Grace deployments by the (unnamed) lead hyperscaler customer, which has said publicly that 'they want to continue to deploy Vera Rubin also as a custom deployment'; Astera aims to stay in that design through the Grace Blackwell to Vera Rubin transition.

contracts.signal: Astera announced a partnership with Microsoft, Intel and SAP so that customers can evaluate Leo CXL memory expansion for their own workloads inside Microsoft Azure M Series virtual machines. Mohan: 'This program represents the industry's first publicly announced deployment of CXL attached memory', with initial production volumes expected to start in 2026.
contracts.date_signed: announced on the Q4 2025 call; production volumes 2026

connects_to.relationship: warrant-linked purchases of Astera smart fabric switches, signal conditioning products and optical engine solutions

contracts.signal: CFO Mike Tate: Astera filed a warrant agreement with Amazon under an 8-K on the call day; it issues 3.3 million warrant shares that vest on performance conditions made up of specified tranches of payments 'to purchase up to $6.5 billion of our smart fabric switches, signal conditioning products, and also our optical engine solutions'. 'It does demonstrate the strong relationship that we have with Amazon.' It is a follow-on to an earlier warrant; warrants are earned as revenue milestones are reached, and Astera is modeling 'a non-cash hit to gross margins of about two points a quarter starting kind of in the Q2 time frame' as they vest, over a seven-year warrant life.
contracts.type: customer warrant agreement tied to purchase milestones

players.product: UALink-based scale-up fabric products (2027) building on Scorpio switch platform

quarterly_data.signal: UALINK ADOPTION SIGNALS FOR 2027: Mohan said UALink traction is building (product announcements, broad IP availability, compliance methodologies being finalized) and cited two public roadmaps - AWS said at re:Invent that the part printed 'Phranyon four' in the transcript, slated to ramp in 2027, will support UALink as well as NVLink Fusion, and AMD said its MI 500 series will support UALink in 2027. Astera will be 'ready to intercept the initial customer platform ramp in 2027'. Asked whether MI 500 is native UALink rather than UALink over Ethernet, he declined to speak for AMD but said AMD's public materials say 'they will continue to support both' and that 'they believe UA Link native is the highest performance scale-up protocol'. On Ethernet scale-up (printed 'ESON'), he expects protocols to coexist ('these solutions will coexist'); Astera could build an Ethernet scale-up part, but 'so far, everybody is telling us to focus on UA Link'. Current development already stretches to 'UV link 200 gig' (as printed).
quarterly_data.figure: UALink platform ramps in 2027 (AWS; AMD MI 500 series)
